html: The Nomlaki are a Wintun people of the west side of the Sacramento Valley and the Coast Range in northern California. Their language lies between that of the Wintu to the north and the Patwin to the south; the Konkow lived across the river to the east. Valley Nomlaki lived in villages near the river, and Hill Nomlaki in the foothills. In 1854 the government set up the Nome Lackee Reservation in their land, one of California's first, but it was broken up within a decade and many were moved to the Round Valley Reservation. Today Nomlaki belong to the Paskenta Band and the Grindstone Rancheria.
